newsitem.title: IRAN: Afghan talks open in Tehran without Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Afghan talks open in Tehran without Taleban.

text.p: A conference to secure peace between warring factions in Afghanistan began in Tehran on Saturday without the participation of the Islamic Taleban militia.
"We regret that not all Afghan groups participated," Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said in his opening speech.

The conference is the latest Iranian initiative for peace in neighbouring Afghanistan where the Taleban, who drove out president Burhanuddin Rabbani's government in September, has made major military gains in the past week.
Rabbani, ousted prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and former president Sibghatullah Mojadedi arrived in Tehran earlier this week for the talks.
Taleban said on Friday the militia had not received any formal invitation for the talks.

"Even if we get an invitation, we will not participate in this conference because Iran is not neutral, it favours one side," Mullah Abddul Jalil, the Taleban's acting deputy foreign minister told a Pakistan-based news service.

Iran, which recognises Rabbani's government, has often criticised the Sunni Moslem aleban for giving Islam a bad name. Iranian media have blasted the Taleban as being set up by Pakistan and backed by Washington. Pakistan denies the charge.
A leader of the Taleban militia said on Saturday that opposition groups must accept it as the country's government as a condition for peace talks.
Attempts by the United Nations and Pakistan have failed to reconcile the Taleban and Rabbani's government. No country has formally recognised the Taleban government.
